/booknotes/12-rules-for-life.metaTitle: 12 Rules for Life – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/12-rules-for-life.metaDescription: My notes on 12 Rules for Life by Jordan Peterson. It mostly comes down to keeping order in your life, because without it things fall apart.

/booknotes/7-habits.metaTitle: 7 Habits of Highly Effective People – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/7-habits.metaDescription: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People by Stephen Covey is the best self-help book I know of. Notes on why the principles hold up.
/booknotes/7-habits.ogImageAlt: 7 Habits of Highly Effective People book cover

/booknotes/a-guide-to-the-good-life.metaTitle: A Guide to the Good Life – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/a-guide-to-the-good-life.metaDescription: William Irvine's introduction to Stoicism. Staying resilient against the outside world, preparing for the worst, content with whatever happens.
/booknotes/a-guide-to-the-good-life.ogImageAlt: A Guide to the Good Life book cover
keywords: A Guide to the Good Life

/booknotes/a-new-kind-of-science.metaTitle: A New Kind of Science – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/a-new-kind-of-science.metaDescription: Stephen Wolfram's case for a science built on computational rules instead of mathematical ones. Proving things by programming them.
/booknotes/a-new-kind-of-science.ogImageAlt: A New Kind of Science book cover

/booknotes/algorithms-to-live-by.metaTitle: Algorithms to Live By – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/algorithms-to-live-by.metaDescription: Optimal stopping, explore versus exploit, sorting. Notes on how Christian and Griffiths map computer science onto everyday decisions.
/booknotes/algorithms-to-live-by.ogImageAlt: Algorithms to Live By book cover

/booknotes/all-about-love.metaTitle: All About Love – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/all-about-love.metaDescription: bell hooks on how the word love lost its meaning, and how it gets used to cover for behaviour that is not loving at all.

/booknotes/almanack-of-naval-ravikant.metaTitle: Almanack of Naval Ravikant – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/almanack-of-naval-ravikant.metaDescription: One of the best books I have read and one I keep going back to. Naval Ravikant on wealth, happiness and thinking from first principles.
/booknotes/almanack-of-naval-ravikant.ogImageAlt: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant book cover

/booknotes/anthem.metaTitle: Anthem by Ayn Rand – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/anthem.metaDescription: A short dystopia where individuality is repressed so thoroughly that people have forgotten the word I. My notes on Anthem by Ayn Rand.

/booknotes/antifragile.metaDescription: Taleb on the difference between fragile and antifragile systems, and why some things get better when you shake them.

/booknotes/anything-you-want.metaTitle: Anything You Want – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/anything-you-want.metaDescription: Derek Sivers on running a business around what is fun and meaningful rather than what counts as industry standard. 40 short lessons.

/booknotes/art-and-artist.metaTitle: Art and Artist – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/art-and-artist.metaDescription: Otto Rank on where the urge to make art comes from, and the tension between the work and the person making it.

/booknotes/atlas-shrugged.metaDescription: Ayn Rand's argument that rational egoism is a virtue, wrapped into a very long and very gripping novel. Out of egoism flows altruism.

/booknotes/atomic-habits.metaDescription: James Clear on making good habits easy and bad habits hard. A lot of this ended up in my own productivity system.

/booknotes/awareness.metaTitle: Awareness by Anthony de Mello – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/awareness.metaDescription: Anthony de Mello on waking up, dropping the identification with your desires and being honest about how selfish we actually are.

/booknotes/behave.metaTitle: Behave by Robert Sapolsky – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/behave.metaDescription: Hands down one of the best books I have ever read. Robert Sapolsky on the biology of human behaviour, from a firing neuron to evolution.

/booknotes/being-you.metaTitle: Being You by Anil Seth – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/being-you.metaDescription: Anil Seth treats consciousness as something measurable. Integrated Information Theory and the Free Energy Principle, and where both fall short.

/booknotes/better-angels.metaTitle: Better Angels of Our Nature – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/better-angels.metaDescription: Steven Pinker's argument that violence has been in decline for centuries, and the data he uses to back it up.
/booknotes/better-angels.ogImageAlt: The Better Angels of Our Nature book cover

/booknotes/bhagavad-gita.metaTitle: Bhagavad Gita – Rico's Book Notes & Key Takeaways
/booknotes/bhagavad-gita.metaDescription: One of the most influential books in history, and worth reading for that alone. Notes on Stephen Mitchell's Bhagavad Gita translation.

/booknotes/black-swan.metaTitle: The Black Swan – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/black-swan.metaDescription: Taleb at his best. The turkey that predicts the future from past data right up until Thanksgiving, and why we are the turkey.

/booknotes/blink.metaTitle: Blink by Malcolm Gladwell – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/blink.metaDescription: Malcolm Gladwell on snap judgements. The same ground Kahneman covers in Thinking Fast and Slow, with more stories and fewer insights.

/booknotes/blood-music.metaTitle: Blood Music by Greg Bear – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/blood-music.metaDescription: Greg Bear writes some of the best sci-fi out there and this is some of his best. Biotechnology, alien intelligence and what counts as human.

/booknotes/brave-new-world.metaTitle: Brave New World – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/brave-new-world.metaDescription: Huxley's dystopia runs on comfort rather than fear. Everybody is happy, drugged on Soma and engineered into their place.

/booknotes/built-to-last.metaTitle: Built to Last – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/built-to-last.metaDescription: Jim Collins looked at companies that lasted to work out what they share. The business idea matters less than the team and the culture.

/booknotes/but-how-do-it-know.metaTitle: But How Do It Know? – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/but-how-do-it-know.metaDescription: J. Clark Scott strips away the abstractions and explains what a computer actually does, starting from logic gates.
/booknotes/but-how-do-it-know.ogImageAlt: But How Do It Know? book cover

/booknotes/chaos.metaTitle: Chaos: Making a New Science – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/chaos.metaDescription: James Gleick's history of chaos theory. Where the field came from, and how non-linear dynamics turn up all over the place.

/booknotes/charlies-almanack.metaTitle: Poor Charlie's Almanack – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/charlies-almanack.metaDescription: Charlie Munger's main point is that you need strong mental models to deal with the world. Close to what Ray Dalio argues in Principles.

/booknotes/complexity.metaTitle: Complexity by Mitchell Waldrop – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/complexity.metaDescription: Heavy on the history of the Santa Fe Institute, lighter on complexity theory than I had hoped. Good on the people who built the field.

/booknotes/creativity-inc.metaDescription: This book moved me. Ed Catmull on how Pixar built a culture where honest feedback and repeated failure end up producing good films.

/booknotes/deep-work.metaTitle: Deep Work by Cal Newport – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/deep-work.metaDescription: Cal Newport on the work that matters most and is hardest to make time for. Useful, though it takes a whole book to say it.

/booknotes/der-steppenwolf.metaDescription: I read this one in German, so half my notes are in German too. The Magical Theater and its alternate versions of a life stuck with me.

/booknotes/der-weg-zum-glueck.metaTitle: Der Weg zum Glück (Dalai Lama) – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/der-weg-zum-glueck.metaDescription: The Dalai Lama on compassion and contentment, and on how much of a hectic life we bring on ourselves. Notes on the German edition.
/booknotes/der-weg-zum-glueck.ogImageAlt: Der Weg zum Glück book cover

/booknotes/determined.metaTitle: Determined by Robert Sapolsky – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/determined.metaDescription: Robert Sapolsky's case against free will, and what follows for blame, praise and the legal system if he turns out to be right.

/booknotes/discourses-and-selected-writi.metaTitle: Discourses by Epictetus – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/discourses-and-selected-writi.metaDescription: Epictetus on responsibility, virtue and knowing what is actually in your control. Practical rather than abstract, like most Stoic writing.
/booknotes/discourses-and-selected-writi.ogImageAlt: Discourses and Selected Writings book cover

/booknotes/disturbing-the-universe.metaTitle: Disturbing the Universe – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/disturbing-the-universe.metaDescription: Freeman Dyson's autobiography. Los Alamos alongside Feynman, and a physicist's ideas about what science might still produce.

/booknotes/drive.metaTitle: Drive by Daniel Pink – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/drive.metaDescription: Daniel Pink on why intrinsic motivation beats carrots and sticks for most modern work. He calls it motivation 3.0.

/booknotes/einsteins-dreams.metaDescription: Truly wonderful, and a quick read. Thirty short stories about universes where time works differently, written almost as poetry.

/booknotes/elon-musk.metaTitle: Elon Musk by Ashley Vance – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/elon-musk.metaDescription: Ashley Vance's biography of Elon Musk. If you want an amazing future you have to go and build it yourself, no matter what it takes.

/booknotes/ending-aging.metaDescription: Aubrey de Grey treats aging as an engineering problem. Seven kinds of damage that accumulate, and what it would take to repair each one.

/booknotes/engines-of-creation.metaTitle: Engines of Creation – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/engines-of-creation.metaDescription: Eric Drexler on what becomes possible once atomic manufacturing works. Structures built from carbon, as strong as diamond.

/booknotes/enough.metaTitle: Enough by John Bogle – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/enough.metaDescription: The Vanguard founder on what got lost when finance dropped its character values, and on knowing when you have enough.

/booknotes/essentialism.metaTitle: Essentialism by Greg McKeown – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/essentialism.metaDescription: The title does most of the work. Declutter your life down to what you actually want, then want fewer things than that.

/booknotes/ethics.metaTitle: Ethics by Spinoza – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/ethics.metaDescription: Spinoza's Ethics, laid out like a geometry proof. God as nature, and human freedom as understanding the order of things.

/booknotes/finite-and-infinite-games.metaTitle: Finite and Infinite Games – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/finite-and-infinite-games.metaDescription: James Carse splits everything humans do into two kinds of game. Finite ones you play to win, infinite ones you play to keep playing.
/booknotes/finite-and-infinite-games.ogImageAlt: Finite and Infinite Games book cover

/booknotes/flow.metaTitle: Flow by Csikszentmihalyi – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/flow.metaDescription: Chess, climbing, coding, skiing, conversation. All of them can put you in the same state, and Csikszentmihalyi explains why.

/booknotes/foundation-1-foundation.metaTitle: Foundation by Isaac Asimov – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/foundation-1-foundation.metaDescription: Part one. A mathematician works out that the galactic empire is about to fall, and sets up a Foundation to keep knowledge alive.

/booknotes/foundation-2-foundation-and-e.metaTitle: Foundation and Empire – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/foundation-2-foundation-and-e.metaDescription: Book two. The dying Empire and the rising Foundation fight over power, and a new ruler looks like he might actually win it.

/booknotes/foundation-3-second-foundatio.metaDescription: Book three. Hari Seldon may have set up a second, hidden Foundation, and the people in it are rumoured to have mind-reading powers.

/booknotes/foundation-4-foundations-edge.metaDescription: Book four. The Second Foundation suspects some other power is quietly helping the Seldon Plan along, and sends a mission to find out.

/booknotes/foundation-5-foundation-and-e.metaTitle: Foundation and Earth – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/foundation-5-foundation-and-e.metaDescription: Book five. If humanity spread out from a single planet, that planet is still out there somewhere. So they go looking for Earth.

/booknotes/foundation-6-prelude-to-found.metaTitle: Prelude to Foundation – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/foundation-6-prelude-to-found.metaDescription: Book six, and a prequel. Hari Seldon invents psychohistory and promptly becomes a problem the Galactic Emperor would like to own.

/booknotes/foundation-7-forward-the-foun.metaTitle: Forward the Foundation – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/foundation-7-forward-the-foun.metaDescription: The last of the seven Foundation novels. Seldon builds his plan and loses everyone close to him while galactic politics grind on.

/booknotes/free-agents.metaDescription: Kevin Mitchell on how evolution produced creatures that make choices for their own reasons, and why that counts as free will.

/booknotes/from-bacteria-to-bach-and-bac.metaTitle: From Bacteria to Bach and Back – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/from-bacteria-to-bach-and-bac.metaDescription: How does physics give rise to life, and life to minds that understand things? Dennett's short answer is evolution. The long answer is the book.
/booknotes/from-bacteria-to-bach-and-bac.ogImageAlt: From Bacteria to Bach and Back book cover
keywords: From Bacteria to Bach and Back

/booknotes/godel-escher-bach.metaTitle: Gödel, Escher, Bach – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/godel-escher-bach.metaDescription: One of my favourite books of all time. Tough to read, harder to summarise, worth re-reading. The tortoise dialogues alone justify it.

/booknotes/godels-proof.metaDescription: Nagel and Newman explain the incompleteness theorem in about a hundred pages. Some true statements can never be proved inside the system.

/booknotes/good-to-great.metaTitle: Good to Great – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/good-to-great.metaDescription: Jim Collins went looking for what great companies have in common. Level 5 leadership, the hedgehog concept, disciplined execution.

/booknotes/grit.metaTitle: Grit by Angela Duckworth – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/grit.metaDescription: One idea, examined from every angle. Persistence, perseverance, resilience, or as the Finns call it, sisu. Angela Duckworth on why it matters.

/booknotes/growth.metaTitle: Growth by Vaclav Smil – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/growth.metaDescription: Vaclav Smil on how things grow, from microorganisms to megacities, and where the biosphere puts a ceiling on all of it.

/booknotes/guns-germs-and-steel.metaTitle: Guns, Germs, and Steel – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/guns-germs-and-steel.metaDescription: One question, book length. Why did Europe pull ahead when older civilisations existed elsewhere? Jared Diamond's answer is geography.
/booknotes/guns-germs-and-steel.ogImageAlt: Guns, Germs, and Steel book cover

/booknotes/hallucinations.metaTitle: Hallucinations by Oliver Sacks – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/hallucinations.metaDescription: Oliver Sacks on perceptions that nobody else can share. Where the line runs between illusion, misperception and hallucination.

/booknotes/hell-yeah-or-no.metaTitle: Hell Yeah or No – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/hell-yeah-or-no.metaDescription: Derek Sivers on small ideas with outsized effects. Working out what you actually want, and why you want it, before committing to anything.
/booknotes/hell-yeah-or-no.ogImageAlt: Hell Yeah or No book cover

/booknotes/high-output-management.metaTitle: High Output Management – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/high-output-management.metaDescription: Andy Grove on managing knowledge workers. Not very applicable to me right now since I manage nobody, so I will come back to it in a few years.

/booknotes/how-to-live.metaTitle: How to Live by Derek Sivers – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/how-to-live.metaDescription: Derek Sivers gives 27 answers to the question of how to live, and every one of them contradicts the last. Which is the point.

/booknotes/how-to-read-a-book.metaTitle: How to Read a Book – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/how-to-read-a-book.metaDescription: Mortimer Adler on reading for insight rather than to pass the time. Four levels of reading, each digging further into the text.
/booknotes/how-to-read-a-book.ogImageAlt: How to Read a Book book cover

/booknotes/how-to-solve-it.metaTitle: How to Solve It – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/how-to-solve-it.metaDescription: Polya's problem-solving strategies, taught through mathematical puzzles. Whether the skill can be taught by a book at all is another question.
/booknotes/how-to-solve-it.ogImageAlt: How to Solve It book cover

/booknotes/how-to-travel-the-world-on-50.metaTitle: How to Travel the World on $50 a Day – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/how-to-travel-the-world-on-50.metaDescription: Worth it if you have not yet had the realisation that travelling can cost less than staying home. Less so once you already travel cheap.
/booknotes/how-to-travel-the-world-on-50.ogImageAlt: How to Travel the World on $50 a Day book cover
keywords: How to Travel the World on 50 a Day

/booknotes/how-to-win-friends-and-influe.metaTitle: How to Win Friends and Influence People – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/how-to-win-friends-and-influe.metaDescription: One of the best self-help books there is, badly served by its title. It is about genuinely caring about people, not manipulating them.
/booknotes/how-to-win-friends-and-influe.ogImageAlt: How to Win Friends and Influence People book cover
keywords: How to Win Friends and Influence People

/booknotes/immune.metaTitle: Immune by Philipp Dettmer – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/immune.metaDescription: Philipp Dettmer of Kurzgesagt on how the immune system works. Which cells do what, and how mindbogglingly complex the whole thing is.

/booknotes/indistractable.metaTitle: Indistractable by Nir Eyal – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/indistractable.metaDescription: Nir Eyal on holding on to your attention in a world built to take it. Mostly about spending less time mindlessly plugged into media.

/booknotes/influence.metaTitle: Influence by Robert Cialdini – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/influence.metaDescription: Cialdini's six principles of persuasion. Reciprocity, commitment, social proof, authority, liking and scarcity, and why we say yes to them.

/booknotes/innate.metaTitle: Innate by Kevin Mitchell – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/innate.metaDescription: Kevin Mitchell on how far genes shape personality and intelligence, and more interestingly, on how we know that in the first place.

/booknotes/intelligence.metaTitle: Intelligence by Osho – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/intelligence.metaDescription: Osho argues that intelligence is part of nature, and that people are made stupid by systems that want to rule them. Meditation as the way back.

/booknotes/lessons-in-psychomagic.metaTitle: Turn Your Life into Art – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/lessons-in-psychomagic.metaDescription: Caveat Magister on designing experiences that change the direction of someone's life by engaging the parts of them they do not control.
/booknotes/lessons-in-psychomagic.ogImageAlt: Turn Your Life into Art book cover

/booknotes/letters-from-a-stoic.metaTitle: Letters from a Stoic – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/letters-from-a-stoic.metaDescription: Seneca on taking whatever the world throws at you without complaint. Staying put, re-reading the same books, being content with less.
/booknotes/letters-from-a-stoic.ogImageAlt: Letters from a Stoic book cover

/booknotes/life-3-0.metaTitle: Life 3.0 by Max Tegmark – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/life-3-0.metaDescription: Max Tegmark on AI safety and machines that outstrip us. He thinks that could happen sooner than expected, so we should start now.

/booknotes/life-the-universe-and-everyth.metaTitle: Life, the Universe and Everything – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/life-the-universe-and-everyth.metaDescription: Book three of the Hitchhiker's Guide. Arthur Dent, the murderous robots of Krikkit and a plot that turns on the game of cricket.
/booknotes/life-the-universe-and-everyth.ogImageAlt: Life, the Universe and Everything book cover

/booknotes/lying.metaTitle: Lying by Sam Harris – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/lying.metaDescription: A very short book by Sam Harris, maybe an hour to read, so these notes are short too. Even small lies cost more than they are worth.

/booknotes/man-and-his-symbols.metaTitle: Man and His Symbols – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/man-and-his-symbols.metaDescription: Jung on symbols and everywhere they turn up. Dreams, art, culture, conversation, the way people arrange their whole lives.
/booknotes/man-and-his-symbols.ogImageAlt: Man and His Symbols book cover

/booknotes/mans-search-for-meaning.metaTitle: Man's Search for Meaning – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/mans-search-for-meaning.metaDescription: Viktor Frankl on surviving the camps and what he took from it. Mostly it puts into perspective how good life is, almost all of the time.
/booknotes/mans-search-for-meaning.ogImageAlt: Man's Search for Meaning book cover

/booknotes/manual-for-living.metaTitle: Manual for Living – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/manual-for-living.metaDescription: The Enchiridion, short and blunt. Epictetus on inner peace, self-mastery and only caring about the things you can actually control.

/booknotes/map-and-territory.metaTitle: Map and Territory – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/map-and-territory.metaDescription: Eliezer Yudkowsky on rationality. How the map in your head relates to the territory, and the biases that pull the two apart.

/booknotes/meditations.metaTitle: Meditations by Marcus Aurelius – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/meditations.metaDescription: The mind is yours to control, the world is not. Marcus Aurelius on getting happy from the inside out, written for nobody but himself.

/booknotes/memos-from-the-chairman.metaTitle: Memos from the Chairman – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/memos-from-the-chairman.metaDescription: A disappointment. I expected wisdom on running a company and got passive-aggressive joke memos from the chairman of Bear Stearns.
/booknotes/memos-from-the-chairman.ogImageAlt: Memos from the Chairman book cover

/booknotes/mind-and-cosmos.metaTitle: Mind and Cosmos – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/mind-and-cosmos.metaDescription: Thomas Nagel argues consciousness has to be fundamental. Something like an atom of consciousness that everything else derives from.

/booknotes/mind-children.metaDescription: Hans Moravec on machines that will eventually think and feel the way we do, with a long account of why he thinks intelligence works like that.

/booknotes/mindset.metaTitle: Mindset by Carol Dweck – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/mindset.metaDescription: Two mindsets, growth and fixed. One lets you learn and get better over time, the other has you defending the ground you already hold.

/booknotes/molecular-biology-of-the-cell.metaTitle: Molecular Biology of the Cell – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/molecular-biology-of-the-cell.metaDescription: Working notes from Molecular Biology of the Cell. The Krebs cycle, free energy and entropy, the electron transport chain, functional groups.
/booknotes/molecular-biology-of-the-cell.ogImageAlt: Molecular Biology of the Cell book cover

/booknotes/momo.metaTitle: Momo by Michael Ende – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/momo.metaDescription: One of my favourite books of all time, and it changes meaning as you get older. Michael Ende on savouring things instead of saving time.

/booknotes/mostly-harmless.metaDescription: The last book in the trilogy of five. Darker than the rest, and Douglas Adams ties off most of the loose ends he left lying around.

/booknotes/neuroplasticity.metaDescription: Moheb Costandi on how the brain forms, prunes and reshapes its connections across a whole life, and what that does and does not allow.

/booknotes/nineteen-eighty-four.metaTitle: 1984 by George Orwell – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/nineteen-eighty-four.metaDescription: Where big brother comes from. Orwell's totalitarian state, in which even a disobedient thought is a punishable offence.

/booknotes/notes-from-underground.metaTitle: Notes from Underground – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/notes-from-underground.metaDescription: Dostoevsky's narrator withdraws from life on purpose, because the world is flawed and doing nothing seems like the only honest response.

/booknotes/outliers.metaTitle: Outliers by Malcolm Gladwell – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/outliers.metaDescription: The book that made ten thousand hours a thing. Gladwell on deliberate practice and the hidden advantages behind unusual success.

/booknotes/outlive.metaTitle: Outlive by Peter Attia – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/outlive.metaDescription: Peter Attia on stretching the good decades rather than the last ones. The four horsemen, and how each builds up long before it shows.

/booknotes/oxygen.metaTitle: Oxygen by Nick Lane – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/oxygen.metaDescription: Nick Lane on one molecule and what it did to life on Earth. A mass extinction first, then the energy budget that made complex life possible.

/booknotes/permanent-record.metaTitle: Permanent Record by Edward Snowden – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/permanent-record.metaDescription: Edward Snowden's memoir. How somebody from a patriotic, government-oriented family ended up handing over the evidence of mass surveillance.

/booknotes/permutation-city.metaDescription: Greg Egan's premise is that a simulation complex enough might keep running even after the hardware underneath it is gone. Then it gets stranger.

/booknotes/predictably-irrational.metaDescription: The title does the summarising. People behave irrationally, but there is method in it, and Dan Ariely maps out where the biases sit.

/booknotes/principles.metaTitle: Principles by Ray Dalio – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/principles.metaDescription: Ray Dalio's own history, then his work principles, then his life principles. The last third is the part that was worth the read for me.

/booknotes/remote.metaTitle: Remote by Jason Fried & DHH – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/remote.metaDescription: Fried and Hansson on why remote work suits everyone involved. Mostly a rehash of how 37signals runs itself, but a short one.

/booknotes/rework.metaTitle: Rework by Jason Fried & DHH – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/rework.metaDescription: Building a business from first principles instead of copying how it is normally done. Lean, and openly hostile to meetings and long hours.

/booknotes/robots-and-empire.metaTitle: Robots and Empire – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/robots-and-empire.metaDescription: The novel that bolts Asimov's robot books onto the Foundation series. Robot ethics, and humans spreading out into the galaxy.

/booknotes/rocheworld.metaTitle: Rocheworld by Robert L. Forward – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/rocheworld.metaDescription: Hard sci-fi about a double planet, two worlds orbiting close enough to touch, and the crew of scientists sent out to look at them.

/booknotes/sapiens.metaTitle: Sapiens by Yuval Noah Harari – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/sapiens.metaDescription: Harari on how we got here. Four revolutions do the heavy lifting, starting with the cognitive one and the stories we agreed to believe.

/booknotes/shantaram.metaTitle: Shantaram by Gregory David Roberts – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/shantaram.metaDescription: A man escapes an Australian prison, lands in Bombay and ends up living in the gangster underworld. Wonderful, and mostly about India.

/booknotes/significant-digits.metaDescription: Fan fiction, and a sequel to Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality. Power, rationality and the mess left behind by the original.

/booknotes/six-easy-pieces.metaTitle: Six Easy Pieces – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/six-easy-pieces.metaDescription: Six chapters lifted out of the Feynman Lectures, the accessible ones. Atoms in motion through to how quantum behaviour works.

/booknotes/six-not-so-easy-pieces.metaTitle: Six Not-So-Easy Pieces – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/six-not-so-easy-pieces.metaDescription: The harder companion volume. Relativity, symmetry and spacetime, still in Feynman's voice but no longer a gentle read.

/booknotes/slaughterhouse-five.metaDescription: Billy Pilgrim comes unstuck in time, and Vonnegut writes the firebombing of Dresden as farce because there is no other way to write it.

/booknotes/snow-crash.metaTitle: Snow Crash by Neal Stephenson – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/snow-crash.metaDescription: The book that named the Metaverse. Corporate city states, a pizza-delivering hacker with a sword and a virus that works on language.

/booknotes/snow-falling-on-cedars.metaTitle: Snow Falling on Cedars – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/snow-falling-on-cedars.metaDescription: A murder trial on an island in the Pacific Northwest, and what the war did to the Japanese-American families who lived there.
/booknotes/snow-falling-on-cedars.ogImageAlt: Snow Falling on Cedars book cover

/booknotes/so-long-and-thanks-for-all-th.metaTitle: So Long, and Thanks for All the Fish – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/so-long-and-thanks-for-all-th.metaDescription: Book four. The title is the message the dolphins left before leaving Earth, and Arthur Dent comes home and falls in love.
/booknotes/so-long-and-thanks-for-all-th.ogImageAlt: So Long and Thanks for All the Fish book cover
keywords: So Long and Thanks for All the Fish

/booknotes/starquake.metaTitle: Starquake by Robert L. Forward – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/starquake.metaDescription: The sequel to Dragon's Egg. Life on a neutron star runs so fast that whole civilisations rise and fall while the humans watch.

/booknotes/still-the-mind.metaTitle: Still the Mind by Alan Watts – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/still-the-mind.metaDescription: Alan Watts on giving up the constant striving for control. His main point is that you are not separate from the world in the first place.

/booknotes/structures-or-why-things-dont.metaTitle: Structures by J.E. Gordon – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/structures-or-why-things-dont.metaDescription: J. E. Gordon on why bridges, roofs and churches stay up. Stress, strain and the parts of civil engineering nobody ever thinks about.
/booknotes/structures-or-why-things-dont.ogImageAlt: Structures or Why Things Don't Fall Down book cover

/booknotes/superintelligence.metaTitle: Superintelligence by Nick Bostrom – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/superintelligence.metaDescription: Nick Bostrom works through the ways an AI smarter than us could end badly, and what could plausibly be done about it beforehand.

/booknotes/surely-you-are-joking-mr-feyn.metaTitle: Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/surely-you-are-joking-mr-feyn.metaDescription: Feynman on Feynman. Safecracking at Los Alamos, drumming in Brazil and the curiosity that ran underneath all of it.
/booknotes/surely-you-are-joking-mr-feyn.ogImageAlt: Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman book cover

/booknotes/tao-te-ching.metaTitle: Tao Te Ching – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/tao-te-ching.metaDescription: A small book of very old wisdom. The Tao as the underlying grain of things, and the case for going with it rather than against it.

/booknotes/the-4-hour-work-week.metaDescription: Tim Ferriss on building a business because a business gives you leverage. The four-hour part is marketing, the leverage part is real.

/booknotes/the-alchemist.metaTitle: The Alchemist by Paulo Coelho – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-alchemist.metaDescription: Santiago the shepherd boy goes looking for treasure and finds his Personal Legend instead. A small magical book about travel and purpose.

/booknotes/the-art-of-learning.metaTitle: The Art of Learning – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-art-of-learning.metaDescription: Josh Waitzkin on mastery, from chess prodigy to martial arts champion. What you strive at matters less than the striving itself.
/booknotes/the-art-of-learning.ogImageAlt: The Art of Learning book cover

/booknotes/the-artists-way.metaTitle: The Artist's Way – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-artists-way.metaDescription: Julia Cameron's twelve-week programme for getting unstuck creatively. Morning pages, artist dates and a lot of showing up.

/booknotes/the-beginning-of-infinity.metaTitle: The Beginning of Infinity – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-beginning-of-infinity.metaDescription: This book is simply insane, in the good way. David Deutsch on good explanations and why knowledge has no upper bound.
/booknotes/the-beginning-of-infinity.ogImageAlt: The Beginning of Infinity book cover

/booknotes/the-biology-of-desire.metaTitle: The Biology of Desire – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-biology-of-desire.metaDescription: Marc Lewis argues addiction is not a disease but learning working exactly as designed, in an environment full of superstimuli.
/booknotes/the-biology-of-desire.ogImageAlt: The Biology of Desire book cover

/booknotes/the-body-keeps-the-score.metaTitle: The Body Keeps the Score – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-body-keeps-the-score.metaDescription: Trauma happens to nearly everybody, in different sizes, and it leaves traces in the body. Bessel van der Kolk on what those traces do.
/booknotes/the-body-keeps-the-score.ogImageAlt: The Body Keeps the Score book cover

/booknotes/the-book-on-the-taboo-against.metaTitle: The Book on the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are
/booknotes/the-book-on-the-taboo-against.metaDescription: Alan Watts on the taught illusion that you are separate from the universe, and what falls away once you stop believing it.
/booknotes/the-book-on-the-taboo-against.ogImageAlt: The Book on the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are book cover
keywords: The Book on the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are

/booknotes/the-book-thief.metaTitle: The Book Thief – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-book-thief.metaDescription: One of my favourite books ever. Death narrates the life of a girl growing up with a new family in the middle of Nazi Germany.

/booknotes/the-brain.metaTitle: The Brain by David Eagleman – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-brain.metaDescription: David Eagleman on how the brain builds the person. Constant rewiring, and how much of who you are depends on what happened to you.

/booknotes/the-caves-of-steel.metaTitle: The Caves of Steel – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-caves-of-steel.metaDescription: A detective story with a robot partner, set in Earth's enclosed underground cities. Those cities are the part I still think about.
/booknotes/the-caves-of-steel.ogImageAlt: The Caves of Steel book cover

/booknotes/the-changing-world-order.metaTitle: The Changing World Order – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-changing-world-order.metaDescription: Ray Dalio on the long cycles behind empires and currencies. Rise, peak, decline and the wars that tend to sit around the handover.
/booknotes/the-changing-world-order.ogImageAlt: The Changing World Order book cover

/booknotes/the-diamond-age.metaTitle: The Diamond Age – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-diamond-age.metaDescription: Everybody can print what they want from the feed, the world has sorted itself into tribes, and one girl gets a book that teaches her.

/booknotes/the-dictators-handbook.metaTitle: The Dictator's Handbook – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-dictators-handbook.metaDescription: Leaders keep power by paying off whoever keeps them in power. Works the same way in dictatorships, democracies and companies.

/booknotes/the-double.metaTitle: The Double by Dostoevsky – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-double.metaDescription: A St Petersburg clerk meets a confident version of himself who starts taking over his life. Dostoevsky on identity coming apart.

/booknotes/the-dragons-egg.metaDescription: Humans fly a mission to a neutron star and find life on it. It runs millions of times faster than they do, so history happens while they watch.

/booknotes/the-enigma-of-reason.metaTitle: The Enigma of Reason – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-enigma-of-reason.metaDescription: Sperber and Mercier argue that reason did not evolve to find truth but to win arguments. Which explains rather a lot about our biases.
/booknotes/the-enigma-of-reason.ogImageAlt: The Enigma of Reason book cover

/booknotes/the-evolution-of-everything.metaTitle: The Evolution of Everything – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-evolution-of-everything.metaDescription: Lots of detailed notes here, but I did not like it that much. Ridley covers the same ground better elsewhere, in The Red Queen for instance.
/booknotes/the-evolution-of-everything.ogImageAlt: The Evolution of Everything book cover

/booknotes/the-fabric-of-reality.metaTitle: The Fabric of Reality – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-fabric-of-reality.metaDescription: David Deutsch stitches quantum physics, epistemology, computation and evolution into one explanation of how the world works.
/booknotes/the-fabric-of-reality.ogImageAlt: The Fabric of Reality book cover

/booknotes/the-feynman-lectures.metaTitle: The Feynman Lectures on Physics – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-feynman-lectures.metaDescription: Notes from Feynman's physics lectures. Atoms, forces, energy and the laws underneath, taught by somebody who enjoyed teaching them.

/booknotes/the-fountain-head.metaTitle: The Fountainhead by Ayn Rand – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-fountain-head.metaDescription: Ayn Rand's architect refuses to compromise on his work, and the novel is about what that costs him. Individualism at full volume.

/booknotes/the-general-theory-of-employm.metaTitle: The General Theory – Keynes Book Notes
/booknotes/the-general-theory-of-employm.metaDescription: Keynes's General Theory, the book macroeconomics grew out of. Employment, interest and money, and why demand can fall short.
/booknotes/the-general-theory-of-employm.ogImageAlt: The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money book cover

/booknotes/the-goal.metaTitle: The Goal by Eliyahu Goldratt – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-goal.metaDescription: A business novel about a failing plant. Goldratt uses it to teach the Theory of Constraints, which mostly means finding the bottleneck.

/booknotes/the-happiness-hypothesis.metaTitle: The Happiness Hypothesis – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-happiness-hypothesis.metaDescription: Jonathan Haidt lines up the modern psychology of wellbeing against ancient wisdom, and finds the old writers got there first quite often.

/booknotes/the-hitchhikers-guide-to-the-.metaTitle: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-hitchhikers-guide-to-the-.metaDescription: Writing notes on science fiction feels strange, so this is mostly a collection of quotes I like. The answer, obviously, is 42.
/booknotes/the-hitchhikers-guide-to-the-.ogImageAlt: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy book cover
keywords: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy

/booknotes/the-idea-factory.metaTitle: The Idea Factory by Jon Gertner – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-idea-factory.metaDescription: Jon Gertner on Bell Labs. The transistor, the laser, information theory and the culture that made all of it happen in one building.

/booknotes/the-idiot.metaTitle: The Idiot by Dostoevsky – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-idiot.metaDescription: Prince Myshkin is genuinely good, which turns out to be a serious handicap in Russian high society. Dostoevsky at his most cruel.

/booknotes/the-infinite-game.metaTitle: The Infinite Game – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-infinite-game.metaDescription: Sinek splits games into finite and infinite ones and argues business is the second kind. Same idea as James Carse, rather less sharp.

/booknotes/the-information.metaTitle: The Information by James Gleick – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-information.metaDescription: James Gleick on information, from talking drums to bits. Where the idea came from, and how much of the modern world rests on it.

/booknotes/the-lean-startup.metaTitle: The Lean Startup by Eric Ries – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-lean-startup.metaDescription: Eric Ries on build, measure, learn. Ship something small, find out whether anybody wants it, and only then keep going.

/booknotes/the-little-book-of-common-sen.metaTitle: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-little-book-of-common-sen.metaDescription: John Bogle's argument for low-cost index funds, made repeatedly and with numbers. Picking stocks mostly loses to the market.
/booknotes/the-little-book-of-common-sen.ogImageAlt: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing book cover
keywords: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing

/booknotes/the-man-who-mistook-his-wife-.metaTitle: The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-man-who-mistook-his-wife-.metaDescription: Oliver Sacks's case studies. Strange neurological failures, each of which says something about how a working brain holds together.
/booknotes/the-man-who-mistook-his-wife-.ogImageAlt: The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat book cover
keywords: The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat

/booknotes/the-martian.metaTitle: The Martian by Andy Weir – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-martian.metaDescription: An astronaut gets left behind on Mars and has to science his way out, one problem at a time. Very funny for a survival story.

/booknotes/the-metamorphosis-of-prime-in.metaTitle: The Metamorphosis of Prime Intellect – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-metamorphosis-of-prime-in.metaDescription: An AI takes godlike power and ends all human suffering. The novella is about what is left to do afterwards, and it is not comfortable.
/booknotes/the-metamorphosis-of-prime-in.ogImageAlt: The Metamorphosis of Prime Intellect book cover

/booknotes/the-mind-illuminated.metaTitle: The Mind Illuminated – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-mind-illuminated.metaDescription: John Yates lays meditation out as ten stages, with Buddhist practice on one side and neuroscience on the other. Very much a manual.

/booknotes/the-misbehavior-of-markets.metaTitle: The Misbehavior of Markets – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-misbehavior-of-markets.metaDescription: Mandelbrot on why standard financial models understate risk, and why fractals fit market behaviour better than bell curves do.
/booknotes/the-misbehavior-of-markets.ogImageAlt: The Misbehavior of Markets book cover

/booknotes/the-moral-landscape.metaTitle: The Moral Landscape by Sam Harris – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-moral-landscape.metaDescription: Sam Harris argues that questions about values have right answers, and that science is allowed to go looking for them.

/booknotes/the-myth-of-sisyphus.metaTitle: The Myth of Sisyphus by Albert Camus – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-myth-of-sisyphus.metaDescription: Camus asks whether life is worth living once you accept it has no meaning. He decides yes, and imagines Sisyphus happy.
/booknotes/the-myth-of-sisyphus.ogImageAlt: The Myth of Sisyphus book cover

/booknotes/the-naked-sun.metaTitle: The Naked Sun by Isaac Asimov – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-naked-sun.metaDescription: A murder on Solaria, a planet where people avoid each other so completely that being in the same room counts as an ordeal.

/booknotes/the-neuroscience-of-addiction.metaTitle: The Neuroscience of Addiction – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-neuroscience-of-addiction.metaDescription: Maria Filbey on what happens in the brain during addiction. Close to the research and short on moralising.
/booknotes/the-neuroscience-of-addiction.ogImageAlt: The Neuroscience of Addiction book cover

/booknotes/the-order-of-time.metaTitle: The Order of Time – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-order-of-time.metaDescription: Carlo Rovelli on time as physics, philosophy and experience see it, and how wildly the three disagree. In the first one it barely exists.
/booknotes/the-order-of-time.ogImageAlt: The Order of Time book cover

/booknotes/the-phoenix-project.metaTitle: The Phoenix Project by Gene Kim – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-phoenix-project.metaDescription: A novel about a failing IT department, written to teach DevOps. Flow, bottlenecks and why the deploy always breaks on a Friday.

/booknotes/the-power-of-habit.metaTitle: The Power of Habit by Charles Duhigg – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-power-of-habit.metaDescription: Charles Duhigg on the cue, routine, reward loop, and how the same loop runs inside companies as much as inside people.
/booknotes/the-power-of-habit.ogImageAlt: The Power of Habit book cover

/booknotes/the-power-of-now.metaTitle: The Power of Now by Eckhart Tolle – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-power-of-now.metaDescription: Eckhart Tolle on getting out of your own head and into the present. Repetitive by design, which is either the point or the problem.
/booknotes/the-power-of-now.ogImageAlt: The Power of Now book cover

/booknotes/the-pragmatic-programmer.metaTitle: The Pragmatic Programmer – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-pragmatic-programmer.metaDescription: The classic on software craft. Not about a language or a framework, but about how to work so that the code stays workable.

/booknotes/the-prince.metaTitle: The Prince by Machiavelli – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-prince.metaDescription: Machiavelli's manual for taking and keeping power, written out of the political mess of 16th century Italy. Still uncomfortable reading.

/booknotes/the-psychedelic-explorers-gui.metaTitle: The Psychedelic Explorer's Guide – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-psychedelic-explorers-gui.metaDescription: James Fadiman on taking psychedelics carefully. Protocols, set and setting. What the research supports, and what it does not.
/booknotes/the-psychedelic-explorers-gui.ogImageAlt: The Psychedelic Explorer's Guide book cover

/booknotes/the-red-queen.metaTitle: The Red Queen by Matt Ridley – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-red-queen.metaDescription: Ridley on sexual selection and evolutionary arms races. Every solution creates the next problem, which is Deutsch's point in another key.

/booknotes/the-republic.metaTitle: The Republic by Plato – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-republic.metaDescription: Justice against injustice, and a perfect state built from first principles in which everybody does exactly one job. Plato's dialogue.

/booknotes/the-restaurant-at-the-end-of-.metaTitle: The Restaurant at the End of the Universe – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-restaurant-at-the-end-of-.metaDescription: Book two. Arthur Dent, a restaurant that dines on the end of everything, and the man who actually runs the universe.
/booknotes/the-restaurant-at-the-end-of-.ogImageAlt: The Restaurant at the End of the Universe book cover
keywords: The Restaurant at the End of the Universe

/booknotes/the-righteous-mind.metaTitle: The Righteous Mind by Jonathan Haidt – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-righteous-mind.metaDescription: Jonathan Haidt on why decent people end up on opposite sides of politics. Moral intuitions come first, the reasoning shows up later.

/booknotes/the-robots-of-dawn.metaTitle: The Robots of Dawn by Isaac Asimov – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-robots-of-dawn.metaDescription: Elijah Baley goes to Aurora to investigate a dead robot, and finds a planet of very civilised people who dislike being crowded.
/booknotes/the-robots-of-dawn.ogImageAlt: The Robots of Dawn book cover

/booknotes/the-selfish-gene.metaTitle: The Selfish Gene by Richard Dawkins – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-selfish-gene.metaDescription: Dawkins on evolution from the gene's point of view. Cooperation only pays under narrow conditions, and this is where memes come from.

/booknotes/the-singularity-is-near.metaTitle: The Singularity Is Near – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-singularity-is-near.metaDescription: Kurzweil's argument that technological growth is exponential, and that general AI is the point where the curve goes vertical.
/booknotes/the-singularity-is-near.ogImageAlt: The Singularity Is Near book cover

/booknotes/the-snow-leopard.metaTitle: The Snow Leopard by Peter Matthiessen – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-snow-leopard.metaDescription: Matthiessen walks into the Himalayas looking for a snow leopard and mostly finds himself. Energy as the Tao, and a lot of walking.

/booknotes/the-structure-of-scientific-r.metaTitle: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-structure-of-scientific-r.metaDescription: Kuhn's argument that science does not accumulate steadily. Pressure builds, something breaks, then the paradigm shifts underneath.
/booknotes/the-structure-of-scientific-r.ogImageAlt: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions book cover

/booknotes/the-tipping-point.metaTitle: The Tipping Point – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-tipping-point.metaDescription: Gladwell on how small changes hit critical mass. The Law of the Few, the Stickiness Factor and the Power of Context do the work.

/booknotes/the-unicorn-project.metaTitle: The Unicorn Project – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-unicorn-project.metaDescription: The developer-side companion to The Phoenix Project. What engineers can actually change about the way their organisation works.

/booknotes/the-vital-question.metaTitle: The Vital Question by Nick Lane – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-vital-question.metaDescription: Nick Lane on energy at the origin of life, and why mitochondria explain how complex cells came to exist at all.

/booknotes/the-war-of-art.metaTitle: The War of Art – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-war-of-art.metaDescription: Pressfield calls the enemy Resistance. Fear of failing and fear of succeeding, plus every trick it uses to stop you making anything.
/booknotes/the-war-of-art.ogImageAlt: The War of Art book cover

/booknotes/the-way-of-zen.metaTitle: The Way of Zen by Alan Watts – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-way-of-zen.metaDescription: Alan Watts explaining Zen Buddhism to a Western audience. A good starting point, because he breaks the ideas down without flattening them.
/booknotes/the-way-of-zen.ogImageAlt: The Way of Zen book cover

/booknotes/the-web-of-meaning.metaTitle: The Web of Meaning – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/the-web-of-meaning.metaDescription: Jeremy Lent argues for a worldview built on interconnection and cooperation instead of the competition and extraction we run on now.
/booknotes/the-web-of-meaning.ogImageAlt: The Web of Meaning book cover

/booknotes/thinking-fast-and-slow.metaTitle: Thinking, Fast and Slow – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/thinking-fast-and-slow.metaDescription: Kahneman's two systems. The fast one jumps to conclusions, the slow one checks them, on the rare occasion it can be bothered.
/booknotes/thinking-fast-and-slow.ogImageAlt: Thinking, Fast and Slow book cover

/booknotes/thus-spoke-zarathustra.metaTitle: Thus Spoke Zarathustra – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/thus-spoke-zarathustra.metaDescription: Nietzsche writes philosophy as a novel. The Ubermensch, the will to power and the eternal recurrence, delivered as sermons.

/booknotes/transformer.metaTitle: Transformer by Nick Lane – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/transformer.metaDescription: Nick Lane on the Krebs cycle as the engine underneath everything. Cells as cities, where the traffic is what keeps them alive.

/booknotes/useful-not-true.metaTitle: Useful Not True – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/useful-not-true.metaDescription: Derek Sivers on dropping the demand that a belief be objectively true. Judge it by what it lets you do instead.

/booknotes/vagabonding.metaTitle: Vagabonding by Rolf Potts – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/vagabonding.metaDescription: Rolf Potts on long-term travel. Mostly about simplifying your life enough that the travelling becomes affordable in the first place.

/booknotes/waking-up.metaTitle: Waking Up by Sam Harris – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/waking-up.metaDescription: Sam Harris on spirituality with no religion attached. Meditation, neuroscience and what happens to the sense of self along the way.

/booknotes/walden.metaTitle: Walden by Henry David Thoreau – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/walden.metaDescription: Thoreau moves to a pond, builds a cabin and writes about living simply. Also about being quietly annoyed by everybody else.

/booknotes/wealth-of-nations.metaTitle: The Wealth of Nations – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/wealth-of-nations.metaDescription: Adam Smith on how markets interact and how a country should be governed so that its market works. The book economics grew out of.
/booknotes/wealth-of-nations.ogImageAlt: The Wealth of Nations book cover

/booknotes/what-do-you-care-what-other-p.metaTitle: What Do You Care What Other People Think? – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/what-do-you-care-what-other-p.metaDescription: Feynman's second book of stories. Arline, the Challenger investigation and a long argument for thinking for yourself.
/booknotes/what-do-you-care-what-other-p.ogImageAlt: What Do You Care What Other People Think? book cover
keywords: What Do You Care What Other People Think

/booknotes/when-breath-becomes-air.metaTitle: When Breath Becomes Air – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/when-breath-becomes-air.metaDescription: A neurosurgeon gets a terminal diagnosis and writes about what is left. One of the few books that genuinely moved me.
/booknotes/when-breath-becomes-air.ogImageAlt: When Breath Becomes Air book cover

/booknotes/why-we-sleep.metaTitle: Why We Sleep – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/why-we-sleep.metaDescription: Matthew Walker on sleep as probably the single biggest contributor to a good life that we know of. Everything gets worse without it.

/booknotes/why-zebras-dont-get-ulcers.metaTitle: Why Zebras Don't Get Ulcers – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/why-zebras-dont-get-ulcers.metaDescription: Sapolsky on the biology of stress. Built for a lion chasing you, badly suited to a mortgage that never quite goes away.
/booknotes/why-zebras-dont-get-ulcers.ogImageAlt: Why Zebras Don't Get Ulcers book cover

/booknotes/your-music-and-people.metaTitle: Your Music and People – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/your-music-and-people.metaDescription: Derek Sivers on making a career in music by being professional and human at once. Useful well outside of music as well.
/booknotes/your-music-and-people.ogImageAlt: Your Music and People book cover

/booknotes/zen-and-the-art.metaTitle: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance – Rico's Booknotes
/booknotes/zen-and-the-art.metaDescription: Pirsig on Quality, and on art and engineering being the same activity seen from two sides. Framed as a motorcycle trip.
/booknotes/zen-and-the-art.ogImageAlt: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance book cover
keywords: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance

/booknotes/zero-to-one.metaTitle: Zero to One by Peter Thiel – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/zero-to-one.metaDescription: One of the best books in existence. Peter Thiel on how startups actually work, why good ideas matter and why you build the future yourself.

/booknotes/zorba-the-greek.metaTitle: Zorba the Greek by Nikos Kazantzakis – Rico's Book Notes
/booknotes/zorba-the-greek.metaDescription: Zorba lives entirely in the present and the narrator cannot manage it. Kazantzakis on appetite, freedom and being embarrassed by both.

/newsletters/sketchplanations-ai-and-arm.metaTitle: Live and Learn #1 – Sketchplanations, AI & Armageddon
/newsletters/sketchplanations-ai-and-arm.metaDescription: The very first edition. Booknotes on Naval Ravikant, morning meditation, an update on Fractal Garden and a pile of links.
/newsletters/sketchplanations-ai-and-arm.ogImageAlt: mountain lake in the italian alps

/newsletters/clippy-resetting-the-loop-a.metaTitle: Live and Learn #2 – Clippy, Resetting the Loop & Complexity
/newsletters/clippy-resetting-the-loop-a.metaDescription: What I learned building Fractal Garden, an explanation of the Krebs cycle, Midjourney generations and links on AI and biochemistry.

/newsletters/creativity-alpha-tensor-and.metaTitle: Live and Learn #3 – Creativity, AlphaTensor & Motivation
/newsletters/creativity-alpha-tensor-and.metaDescription: Booknotes on Creativity Inc., DeepMind's AlphaTensor paper and a handful of links on motivation and getting things done.
/newsletters/creativity-alpha-tensor-and.ogImageAlt: Portal door leading into the forest

/newsletters/collision-detection-synthet.metaTitle: Live and Learn #4 – Collision Detection, Synbio & AI
/newsletters/collision-detection-synthet.metaDescription: Booknotes on Indistractable, Michael Levin on Lex Fridman, Sam Altman on what comes next and collision detection in code.
/newsletters/collision-detection-synthet.ogImageAlt: Tornado storm clouds with lightning strikes hovering over a field in the meadow

/newsletters/richard-feynman-ambition-an.metaTitle: Live and Learn #5 – Richard Feynman, Ambition & Sound
/newsletters/richard-feynman-ambition-an.metaDescription: Booknotes on Lying by Sam Harris, a timelapse of a salamander growing, travel photos and some physics along the way.
/newsletters/richard-feynman-ambition-an.ogImageAlt: leaves with little, sparkling water droplets

/newsletters/chat-gpt-neuralink-and-advi.metaTitle: Live and Learn #6 – ChatGPT, Neuralink & Procrastination
/newsletters/chat-gpt-neuralink-and-advi.metaDescription: A list of the best textbooks, an animated video about the future, new podcast notes and advice for beating procrastination.
/newsletters/chat-gpt-neuralink-and-advi.ogImageAlt: futuristic city, with lightning striking the skies

/newsletters/3-d-in-the-browser-neurons-.metaTitle: Live and Learn #7 – 3D in the Browser & Neurons in a Dish
/newsletters/3-d-in-the-browser-neurons-.metaDescription: Rules for life, work and health, neurons growing in a petri dish, low-level networking tutorials and the beauty of splines.

/newsletters/computational-selves-min-d-.metaTitle: Live and Learn #8 – Computational Selves, MinDVis & AI
/newsletters/computational-selves-min-d-.metaDescription: Eric Schmidt, a story about what an AI takeoff might actually look like, and a paper on the theory of computational selves.

/now.ogImageAlt: A moment in time representing the now page concept

/principles.metaTitle: My Principles - Rules for a Happy and Fulfilled Life
/principles.metaDescription: A list of principles I try to live by. Fighting procrastination, investing in relationships and carrying on learning.
